paper_metadata.title: Quantum Circuits for the Black-Scholes equations via Schrödingerisation

experiments.description: Qiskit statevector-based numerical verification of the 1D Black-Scholes Schrödingerisation circuit for a European call option, comparing two initial conditions and varying ancilla size np and spatial resolution nx.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation for 1D Black-Scholes equation with Trotter splitting and warped phase transformation

initial_conditions: u0 = w0 - e^x with w0 = max(e^x - K, 0)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from the discretized option payoff; second experiment uses smoother p-dimension initial function g(p).

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discretized spatial grid in x encoded on nx qubits; auxiliary p register encoded on np qubits; total state prepared as |u> or |v> over the discretized grid.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the transformed Black-Scholes PDE ∂u/∂τ = (r - σ^2/2) ∂u/∂x + (σ^2/2) ∂^2u/∂x^2 - r u with boundary conditions and recover option price.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Dirichlet boundary conditions handled by finite-difference discretization; Schrödingerisation uses dilation with auxiliary variable R(t) and post-selection on p > 0.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_BS = C1 ⊗ D_eta + C2 ⊗ I^{⊗np}, with C1 and C2 defined from the dilated system and finite-difference operators H1, H2.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing in 1D Black-Scholes model.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical Black-Scholes benchmark with exact solution u(x,t)=e^x N(d1)-Ke^{-rt}N(d2); evaluated on S in [0,2E] for visualization.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log transform s=e^x; truncate x-domain to [xmin,xmax]; finite-difference discretization in x and p; compare against exact analytical solution and classical matrix-exponential baseline.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Qiskit Statevector simulator for full solution; Estimator for observables; compare numerical solution and error against exact solution and classical finite-difference/matrix-exponential baseline; report CPU runtime and RAM; convergence table for multiple grid refinements.

implementation_details.classical_solver: direct ODE solve via matrix exponential / classical finite difference
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization of the PDE; construction of initial state and auxiliary p-grid.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse QFT and projection onto p > 0 to recover option price; compare against exact analytical solution and classical baseline.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; ˜O(d/ε^3) scaling in high dimensions
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference methods with curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: high-dimensional settings; assuming the Schrödingerisation-based quantum circuit model and asymptotic complexity analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims polynomial advantage in scaling, but the numerical experiment itself is a small-scale simulator study and does not empirically demonstrate asymptotic speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ˜O(T^2 ||u(0)||^3 / (h^4 ε^3 ||u(T)||^3)) for state preparation; circuit simulation cost scales as O(Np T^2 n_x^2 / ε) up to logarithmic factors and problem constants
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical finite-difference methods suffer from curse of dimensionality; for 1D baseline, direct matrix exponential solve is used (no explicit asymptotic bound given).

experiments.description: Qiskit numerical verification of the 2D Black-Scholes Schrödingerisation circuit for a cash-or-nothing option, using a correlated-asset pricing setup and fixed grid sizes.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation for d-dimensional Black-Scholes equation with Trotter splitting
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial condition u0(x,y)=c for x>ln(K1), y>ln(K2), else 0; auxiliary p register initialized as in the Schrödingerisation construction.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two spatial dimensions discretized on nx qubits per asset dimension and an auxiliary p register on np qubits; total register size dnx + np for d=2.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the 2D Black-Scholes PDE with mixed boundary conditions and recover the cash-or-nothing option price.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Mixed boundary conditions: zero at lower boundaries and zero derivative at upper boundaries; Schrödingerisation applied directly without dilation because the option is cash-or-nothing / zero at boundaries.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_BS = A1 ⊗ D_eta + A2 ⊗ I^{⊗np}, with A1 and A2 from the Hermitian/anti-Hermitian decomposition of the finite-difference operator.

problem_instance.description: Two-dimensional cash-or-nothing option pricing under correlated Black-Scholes dynamics.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical benchmark with exact solution u(x,y,τ)=c e^{-rτ} B(d_x,d_y,ρ); evaluated with two initial values similar to the 1D case.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log transform s_i=e^{x_i}; finite-difference discretization in x, y, and p; mixed boundary conditions; compare numerical solution to exact analytical solution.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Matlab/Qiskit-based numerical simulation; report solution plots for two initial values; no explicit shot-based sampling reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: analytical exact solution / classical finite-difference reference
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization of the 2D PDE and construction of initial condition.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse QFT and projection onto p > 0 to recover the option price; compare with exact solution and plot upper-right in figures.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; ˜O(d/ε^3) scaling in high dimensions
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference methods with exponential scaling in dimension O(N_x^d)
speedup_claims.conditions: high-dimensional settings; assuming the Schrödingerisation-based quantum circuit model and asymptotic complexity analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: The 2D numerical example validates correctness on a simulator but does not empirically measure asymptotic speedup.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical finite-difference methods scale exponentially in dimension as O(N_x^d) in the discussion.
